title: Specify closing the select picker when it can no longer be shown
body:
A select's picker can only be shown while the select is a drop-down box with base appearance and its select popover also has base appearance. If that stops being true while the picker is showing, implementations close the picker, but HTML doesn't say so or when. This happens, for example, through `select:open { appearance: auto }`, which would otherwise be circular, or when script sets `size`.

Chromium closes it during style recalc when the select's appearance changes, so `getComputedStyle()` can close it. When the picker's appearance changes, it closes it in a task instead. WebKit closes it in a task in both cases.

The focus fixup rule handles the same kind of style-driven change as a step of update the rendering, and I suggest doing that here too. Right before the focus fixup rule, add: for each `select` whose select popover is showing, and which is not being rendered as a drop-down box with base appearance or whose select popover is not being rendered with base appearance, run the hide popover algorithm given its select popover, false, false, false, and null.

`switch-picker-appearance.html` in WPT assumed Chromium's synchronous close for one case. WebKit will export a version that waits for a rendering update, plus `switch-picker-appearance-timing.tentative.html` for this proposal.
